text:
sara_infra: heads up — several gpu nodes in us-west-2 are NotReady and a bunch of inference pods are CrashLooping. kubelet logs show liveness probe timeouts. suspect networking change. anyone touching NACLs/SGs on the edge subnets?

mike_netops: not me this morning. did we have any recent terraform updates to prod VPC rules? :thinking_face:

ana_sre: i saw a deploy-bot alert around 09:04 for a security rule change but didnt inspect. deploy-bot, can you paste the change?

deploy-bot: Config change applied by @tim_ops at 2026-03-18T09:04:12Z:
```
change: network_acl.rule[45].egress = "deny tcp 1024-65535" -> "deny"\nreason: tighten ephemeral port range for security audit
```

tim_ops: that was my change — we tightened ephemeral egress on the edge NACL to lock down lateral traffic. i thought only management subnets were impacted. sorry if it hit GPU subnets.

jordan_platform: oh that explains it. our kube-probes originate from node local proxies on high ephemeral ports (TCP 32768+). if egress is blocked, node -> kube-apiserver or node -> lb probes fail. can you revert or add exceptions for the subnet range used by gpu nodes?

sara_infra: confirmed with `kubectl get pods -n ml-inference -o wide`: many pods show Node: gpu-usw2-*-*, RESTARTS high. kube-probe logs snippet: 
```
I0302 09:10:05.123456    1234 kuberuntime_manager.go:xxx] liveness probe failed: Get "http://10.0.12.34:10256/healthz": dial tcp 10.0.12.34:10256: i/o timeout
```

mike_netops: quick check — can someone run `aws ec2 describe-network-acls --region us-west-2 --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-xxxx` and `aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=redwood-edge-*`? i suspect NACL egress block, SGs are usually permissive for ephemeral.

tim_ops: running now. output shows NACL rule 100 explicitly DENY egress 1024-65535 for subnet subnet-0a1b2c. that is the gpu pool subnet. my bad.

ana_sre: for quick mitigation, two options: 1) revert the NACL change (fast), 2) add specific ALLOW egress rule for ephemeral ports to the gpu subnet association (non-destructive). which do you prefer?

jordan_platform: prefer option 2 (add allow) so change is minimal. also we should patch docs: kubelet/hc uses node local ports.

tim_ops: adding ALLOW egress 1024-65535 for subnet-0a1b2c now. will apply via cloud console and then push a targeted terraform patch to keep infra in sync.

mike_netops: monitoring metrics — node readiness improving. within 60s i see kubelet success and pods moving to Ready. :thumbsup:

sara_infra: pods are back to running for ml-inference; GPU capacity restored. thanks. can we add an automated smoke check after NACL changes? this caused a 25% drop in available GPU slots.

ana_sre: yes — adding a preflight job that runs `kubectl get nodes` and simple probe to the kubelet ports, fail the infra change if checks fail. i'll open a quick RFC.

tim_ops: will coordinate with infra-change process. again, apologies. lesson: ephemeral-port NACLs are dangerous for node-level probes.

jordan_platform: also will add a short doc in /runbooks/networking about ephemeral port needs for kube-probes and node kube-proxy egress.

mike_netops: closing loop — recommend a scheduled audit to find any other subnets with similar tight rules. i'll run a query across all regions later today.

sara_infra: great. file followups here and mark incident severity low since recovered. thanks everyone.
